components.description: The API server is the front end for the Kubernetes control plane. It exposes the Kubernetes API and handles REST operations.

key_flags.name: --admission-control-config-file
key_flags.description: File with admission control configuration.

key_flags.name: --advertise-address
key_flags.description: The IP address on which to advertise the apiserver to members of the cluster. This address must be reachable by the rest of the cluster. If blank, the --bind-address will be used. If --bind-address is unspecified, the host's default interface will be used.

key_flags.name: --aggregator-reject-forwarding-redirect
key_flags.description: Aggregator reject forwarding redirect response back to client.

key_flags.name: --allow-metric-labels
key_flags.description: The map from metric-label to value allow-list of this label. The key's format is <MetricName>,<LabelName>. The value's format is <allowed_value>,<allowed_value>...e.g. metric1,label1='v1,v2,v3', metric1,label2='v1,v2,v3' metric2,label1='v1,v2,v3'.

key_flags.name: --allow-metric-labels-manifest
key_flags.description: The path to the manifest file that contains the allow-list mapping. The format of the file is the same as the flag --allow-metric-labels. Note that the flag --allow-metric-labels will override the manifest file.

key_flags.name: --allow-privileged
key_flags.description: If true, allow privileged containers. [default=false]

key_flags.name: --anonymous-auth
key_flags.description: Enables anonymous requests to the secure port of the API server. Requests that are not rejected by another authentication method are treated as anonymous requests. Anonymous requests have a username of system:anonymous, and a group name of system:unauthenticated.

key_flags.name: --api-audiences
key_flags.description: Identifiers of the API. The service account token authenticator will validate that tokens used against the API are bound to at least one of these audiences. If the --service-account-issuer flag is configured and this flag is not, this field defaults to a single element list containing the issuer URL.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-batch-buffer-size
key_flags.description: The size of the buffer to store events before batching and writing. Only used in batch mode.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-batch-max-size
key_flags.description: The maximum size of a batch. Only used in batch mode.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-batch-max-wait
key_flags.description: The amount of time to wait before force writing the batch that hadn't reached the max size. Only used in batch mode.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-batch-throttle-burst
key_flags.description: Maximum number of requests sent at the same moment if ThrottleQPS was not utilized before. Only used in batch mode.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-batch-throttle-enable
key_flags.description: Whether batching throttling is enabled. Only used in batch mode.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-batch-throttle-qps
key_flags.description: Maximum average number of batches per second. Only used in batch mode.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-compress
key_flags.description: If set, the rotated log files will be compressed using gzip.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-format
key_flags.description: Format of saved audits. "legacy" indicates 1-line text format for each event. "json" indicates structured json format. Known formats are legacy,json.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-maxage
key_flags.description: The maximum number of days to retain old audit log files based on the timestamp encoded in their filename.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-maxbackup
key_flags.description: The maximum number of old audit log files to retain. Setting a value of 0 will mean there's no restriction on the number of files.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-maxsize
key_flags.description: The maximum size in megabytes of the audit log file before it gets rotated.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-mode
key_flags.description: Strategy for sending audit events. Blocking indicates sending events should block server responses. Batch causes the backend to buffer and write events asynchronously. Known modes are batch,blocking,blocking-strict.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-path
key_flags.description: If set, all requests coming to the apiserver will be logged to this file. '-' means standard out.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-truncate-enabled
key_flags.description: Whether event and batch truncating is enabled.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-truncate-max-batch-size
key_flags.description: Maximum size of the batch sent to the underlying backend. Actual serialized size can be several hundreds of bytes greater. If a batch exceeds this limit, it is split into several batches of smaller size.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-truncate-max-event-size
key_flags.description: Maximum size of the audit event sent to the underlying backend. If the size of an event is greater than this number, first request and response are removed, and if this doesn't reduce the size enough, event is discarded.

key_flags.name: --audit-log-version
key_flags.description: API group and version used for serializing audit events written to log.

key_flags.name: --audit-policy-file
key_flags.description: Path to the file that defines the audit policy configuration.

key_flags.name: --audit-webhook-batch-buffer-size
key_flags.description: The size of the buffer to store events before batching and writing. Only used in batch mode.

key_flags.name: --audit-webhook-batch-max-size
key_flags.description: The maximum size of a batch. Only used in batch mode.

key_flags.name: --audit-webhook-batch-max-wait
key_flags.description: The amount of time to wait before force writing the batch that hadn't reached the max size. Only used in batch mode.

key_flags.name: --audit-webhook-batch-throttle-burst
key_flags.description: Maximum number of requests sent at the same moment if ThrottleQPS was not utilized before. Only used in batch mode.

key_flags.name: --audit-webhook-batch-throttle-enable
key_flags.description: Whether batching throttling is enabled. Only used in batch mode.

key_flags.name: --audit-webhook-batch-throttle-qps
key_flags.description: Maximum average number of batches per second. Only used in batch mode.

key_flags.name: --audit-webhook-config-file
key_flags.description: Path to a kubeconfig formatted file that defines the audit webhook configuration.

key_flags.name: --audit-webhook-initial-backoff
key_flags.description: The amount of time to wait before retrying the first failed request.

key_flags.name: --audit-webhook-mode
key_flags.description: Strategy for sending audit events. Blocking indicates sending events should block server responses. Batch causes the backend to buffer and write events asynchronously. Known modes are batch,blocking,blocking-strict.

key_flags.name: --audit-webhook-truncate-enabled
key_flags.description: Whether event and batch truncating is enabled.

key_flags.name: --audit-webhook-truncate-max-batch-size
key_flags.description: Maximum size of the batch sent to the underlying backend. Actual serialized size can be several hundreds of bytes greater. If a batch exceeds this limit, it is split into several batches of smaller size.

key_flags.name: --audit-webhook-truncate-max-event-size
key_flags.description: Maximum size of the audit event sent to the underlying backend. If the size of an event is greater than this number, first request and response are removed, and if this doesn't reduce the size enough, event is discarded.

key_flags.name: --audit-webhook-version
key_flags.description: API group and version used for serializing audit events written to webhook.

key_flags.name: --authentication-config
key_flags.description: File with Authentication Configuration to configure the JWT Token authenticator or the anonymous authenticator. Requires the StructuredAuthenticationConfiguration feature gate. This flag is mutually exclusive with the --oidc-* flags if the file configures the JWT Token authenticator. This flag is mutually exclusive with --anonymous-auth if the file configures the Anonymous authenticator.

key_flags.name: --authentication-token-webhook-cache-ttl
key_flags.description: The duration to cache responses from the webhook token authenticator.

key_flags.name: --authentication-token-webhook-config-file
key_flags.description: File with webhook configuration for token authentication in kubeconfig format. The API server will query the remote service to determine authentication for bearer tokens.

key_flags.name: --authentication-token-webhook-version
key_flags.description: The API version of the authentication.k8s.io TokenReview to send to and expect from the webhook.

key_flags.name: --authorization-config
key_flags.description: File with Authorization Configuration to configure the authorizer chain. Requires feature gate StructuredAuthorizationConfiguration. This flag is mutually exclusive with the other --authorization-mode and --authorization-webhook-* flags.

key_flags.name: --authorization-mode
key_flags.description: Ordered list of plug-ins to do authorization on secure port. Defaults to AlwaysAllow if --authorization-config is not used. Comma-delimited list of: AlwaysAllow,AlwaysDeny,ABAC,Webhook,RBAC,Node.

key_flags.name: --authorization-policy-file
key_flags.description: File with authorization policy in json line by line format, used with --authorization-mode=ABAC, on the secure port.

key_flags.name: --authorization-webhook-cache-authorized-ttl
key_flags.description: The duration to cache 'authorized' responses from the webhook authorizer.

key_flags.name: --authorization-webhook-cache-unauthorized-ttl
key_flags.description: The duration to cache 'unauthorized' responses from the webhook authorizer.

key_flags.name: --authorization-webhook-config-file
key_flags.description: File with webhook configuration in kubeconfig format, used with --authorization-mode=Webhook. The API server will query the remote service to determine access on the API server's secure port.

key_flags.name: --authorization-webhook-version
key_flags.description: The API version of the authorization.k8s.io SubjectAccessReview to send to and expect from the webhook.

key_flags.name: --bind-address
key_flags.description: The IP address on which to listen for the --secure-port port. The associated interface(s) must be reachable by the rest of the cluster, and by CLI/web clients. If blank or an unspecified address (0.0.0.0 or ::), all interfaces and IP address families will be used.

key_flags.name: --cert-dir
key_flags.description: The directory where the TLS certs are located. If --tls-cert-file and --tls-private-key-file are provided, this flag will be ignored.

key_flags.name: --client-ca-file
key_flags.description: If set, any request presenting a client certificate signed by one of the authorities in the client-ca-file is authenticated with an identity corresponding to the CommonName of the client certificate.

key_flags.name: --contention-profiling
key_flags.description: Enable block profiling, if profiling is enabled

key_flags.name: --coordinated-leadership-lease-duration
key_flags.description: The duration of the lease used for Coordinated Leader Election.

key_flags.name: --coordinated-leadership-renew-deadline
key_flags.description: The deadline for renewing a coordinated leader election lease.

key_flags.name: --coordinated-leadership-retry-period
key_flags.description: The period for retrying to renew a coordinated leader election lease.

key_flags.name: --cors-allowed-origins
key_flags.description: List of allowed origins for CORS, comma separated. An allowed origin can be a regular expression to support subdomain matching. If this list is empty CORS will not be enabled. Please ensure each expression matches the entire hostname by anchoring to the start with '^' or including the '//' prefix, and by anchoring to the end with '$' or including the ':' port separator suffix. Examples of valid expressions are '//example.com(:|$)' and '^https://example.com(:|$)'

key_flags.name: --debug-socket-path
key_flags.description: Use an unprotected (no authn/authz) unix-domain socket for profiling with the given path

key_flags.name: --default-not-ready-toleration-seconds
key_flags.description: Indicates the tolerationSeconds of the toleration for notReady:NoExecute that is added by default to every pod that does not already have such a toleration.

key_flags.name: --default-unreachable-toleration-seconds
key_flags.description: Indicates the tolerationSeconds of the toleration for unreachable:NoExecute that is added by default to every pod that does not already have such a toleration.

key_flags.name: --delete-collection-workers
key_flags.description: Number of workers spawned for DeleteCollection call. These are used to speed up namespace cleanup.

key_flags.name: --disable-admission-plugins
key_flags.description: admission plugins that should be disabled although they are in the default enabled plugins list (NamespaceLifecycle, LimitRanger, ServiceAccount, TaintNodesByCondition, PodSecurity, Priority, DefaultTolerationSeconds, DefaultStorageClass, StorageObjectInUseProtection, PersistentVolumeClaimResize, RuntimeClass, CertificateApproval, CertificateSigning, ClusterTrustBundleAttest, CertificateSubjectRestriction, DefaultIngressClass, PodTopologyLabels, MutatingAdmissionPolicy, MutatingAdmissionWebhook,

key_flags.name: --disable-http2-serving
key_flags.description: If true, HTTP2 serving will be disabled [default=false]

key_flags.name: --disabled-metrics
key_flags.description: This flag provides an escape hatch for misbehaving metrics. You must provide the fully qualified metric name in order to disable it. Disclaimer: disabling metrics is higher in precedence than showing hidden metrics.

key_flags.name: --egress-selector-config-file
key_flags.description: File with apiserver egress selector configuration.

key_flags.name: --emulated-version
key_flags.description: The versions different components emulate their capabilities (APIs, features, ...) of. If set, the component will emulate the behavior of this version instead of the underlying binary version. Version format could only be major.minor, for example: '--emulated-version=wardle=1.2,kube=1.31'. Options are: kube=1.31..1.34(default:1.34) If the component is not specified, defaults to "kube"

key_flags.name: --emulation-forward-compatible
key_flags.description: If true, for any beta+ APIs enabled by default or by --runtime-config at the emulation version, their future versions with higher priority/stability will be auto enabled even if they introduced after the emulation version. Can only be set to true if the emulation version is lower than the binary version.

key_flags.name: --enable-admission-plugins
key_flags.description: admission plugins that should be enabled in addition to default enabled ones (NamespaceLifecycle, LimitRanger, ServiceAccount, TaintNodesByCondition, PodSecurity, Priority, DefaultTolerationSeconds, DefaultStorageClass, StorageObjectInUseProtection, PersistentVolumeClaimResize, RuntimeClass, CertificateApproval, CertificateSigning, ClusterTrustBundleAttest, CertificateSubjectRestriction, DefaultIngressClass, PodTopologyLabels, MutatingAdmissionPolicy, MutatingAdmissionWebhook, ValidatingAdmissio

key_flags.name: --enable-aggregator-routing
key_flags.description: Turns on aggregator routing requests to endpoints IP rather than cluster IP.

key_flags.name: --enable-bootstrap-token-auth
key_flags.description: Enable to allow secrets of type 'bootstrap.kubernetes.io/token' in the 'kube-system' namespace to be used for TLS bootstrapping authentication.

key_flags.name: --enable-garbage-collector
key_flags.description: Enables the generic garbage collector. MUST be synced with the corresponding flag of the kube-controller-manager.

key_flags.name: --enable-priority-and-fairness
key_flags.description: If true, replace the max-in-flight handler with an enhanced one that queues and dispatches with priority and fairness

key_flags.name: --encryption-provider-config
key_flags.description: The file containing configuration for encryption providers to be used for storing secrets in etcd

key_flags.name: --encryption-provider-config-automatic-reload
key_flags.description: Determines if the file set by --encryption-provider-config should be automatically reloaded if the disk contents change. Setting this to true disables the ability to uniquely identify distinct KMS plugins via the API server healthz endpoints.

key_flags.name: --endpoint-reconciler-type
key_flags.description: Use an endpoint reconciler (master-count, lease, none) master-count is deprecated, and will be removed in a future version.

key_flags.name: --etcd-cafile
key_flags.description: SSL Certificate Authority file used to secure etcd communication.

key_flags.name: --etcd-certfile
key_flags.description: SSL certification file used to secure etcd communication.

key_flags.name: --etcd-compaction-interval
key_flags.description: The interval of compaction requests. If 0, the compaction request from apiserver is disabled.

key_flags.name: --etcd-count-metric-poll-period
key_flags.description: Frequency of polling etcd for number of resources per type. 0 disables the metric collection.

key_flags.name: --etcd-db-metric-poll-interval
key_flags.description: The interval of requests to poll etcd and update metric. 0 disables the metric collection

key_flags.name: --etcd-healthcheck-timeout
key_flags.description: The timeout to use when checking etcd health.

key_flags.name: --etcd-keyfile
key_flags.description: SSL key file used to secure etcd communication.

key_flags.name: --etcd-prefix
key_flags.description: The prefix to prepend to all resource paths in etcd.

key_flags.name: --etcd-readycheck-timeout
key_flags.description: The timeout to use when checking etcd readiness

key_flags.name: --etcd-servers
key_flags.description: List of etcd servers to connect with (scheme://ip:port), comma separated.

key_flags.name: --etcd-servers-overrides
key_flags.description: Per-resource etcd servers overrides, comma separated. The individual override format: group/resource#servers, where servers are URLs, semicolon separated. Note that this applies only to resources compiled into this server binary. e.g. "/pods#http://etcd4:2379;http://etcd5:2379,/events#http://etcd6:2379"

key_flags.name: --event-ttl
key_flags.description: Amount of time to retain events.

key_flags.name: --external-hostname
key_flags.description: The hostname to use when generating externalized URLs for this master (e.g. Swagger API Docs or OpenID Discovery).

key_flags.name: --feature-gates
key_flags.description: Comma-separated list of component:key=value pairs that describe feature gates for alpha/experimental features of different components. If the component is not specified, defaults to "kube". This flag can be repeatedly invoked. For example: --feature-gates 'wardle:featureA=true,wardle:featureB=false' --feature-gates 'kube:featureC=true'Options are: kube:APIResponseCompression=true|false (BETA - default=true) kube:APIServerIdentity=true|false (BETA - default=true) kube:APIServingWithRoutine=true|f

key_flags.name: --goaway-chance
key_flags.description: To prevent HTTP/2 clients from getting stuck on a single apiserver, randomly close a connection (GOAWAY). The client's other in-flight requests won't be affected, and the client will reconnect, likely landing on a different apiserver after going through the load balancer again. This argument sets the fraction of requests that will be sent a GOAWAY. Clusters with single apiservers, or which don't use a load balancer, should NOT enable this. Min is 0 (off), Max is .02 (1/50 requests); .001 (1/1000

key_flags.name: --help
key_flags.description: help for kube-apiserver

key_flags.name: --http2-max-streams-per-connection
key_flags.description: The limit that the server gives to clients for the maximum number of streams in an HTTP/2 connection. Zero means to use golang's default.

key_flags.name: --kubelet-certificate-authority
key_flags.description: Path to a cert file for the certificate authority.

key_flags.name: --kubelet-client-certificate
key_flags.description: Path to a client cert file for TLS.

key_flags.name: --kubelet-client-key
key_flags.description: Path to a client key file for TLS.

key_flags.name: --kubelet-preferred-address-types
key_flags.description: List of the preferred NodeAddressTypes to use for kubelet connections.

key_flags.name: --kubelet-timeout
key_flags.description: Timeout for kubelet operations.

key_flags.name: --kubernetes-service-node-port
key_flags.description: If non-zero, the Kubernetes master service (which apiserver creates/maintains) will be of type NodePort, using this as the value of the port. If zero, the Kubernetes master service will be of type ClusterIP.

key_flags.name: --lease-reuse-duration-seconds
key_flags.description: The time in seconds that each lease is reused. A lower value could avoid large number of objects reusing the same lease. Notice that a too small value may cause performance problems at storage layer.

key_flags.name: --livez-grace-period
key_flags.description: This option represents the maximum amount of time it should take for apiserver to complete its startup sequence and become live. From apiserver's start time to when this amount of time has elapsed, /livez will assume that unfinished post-start hooks will complete successfully and therefore return true.

key_flags.name: --log-flush-frequency
key_flags.description: Maximum number of seconds between log flushes

key_flags.name: --log-text-info-buffer-size
key_flags.description: [Alpha] In text format with split output streams, the info messages can be buffered for a while to increase performance. The default value of zero bytes disables buffering. The size can be specified as number of bytes (512), multiples of 1000 (1K), multiples of 1024 (2Ki), or powers of those (3M, 4G, 5Mi, 6Gi). Enable the LoggingAlphaOptions feature gate to use this.

key_flags.name: --log-text-split-stream
key_flags.description: [Alpha] In text format, write error messages to stderr and info messages to stdout. The default is to write a single stream to stdout. Enable the LoggingAlphaOptions feature gate to use this.

key_flags.name: --logging-format
key_flags.description: Sets the log format. Permitted formats: "text".

key_flags.name: --max-connection-bytes-per-sec
key_flags.description: If non-zero, throttle each user connection to this number of bytes/sec. Currently only applies to long-running requests.

key_flags.name: --max-mutating-requests-inflight
key_flags.description: This and --max-requests-inflight are summed to determine the server's total concurrency limit (which must be positive) if --enable-priority-and-fairness is true. Otherwise, this flag limits the maximum number of mutating requests in flight, or a zero value disables the limit completely.

key_flags.name: --max-requests-inflight
key_flags.description: This and --max-mutating-requests-inflight are summed to determine the server's total concurrency limit (which must be positive) if --enable-priority-and-fairness is true. Otherwise, this flag limits the maximum number of non-mutating requests in flight, or a zero value disables the limit completely.

key_flags.name: --min-request-timeout
key_flags.description: An optional field indicating the minimum number of seconds a handler must keep a request open before timing it out. Currently only honored by the watch request handler, which picks a randomized value above this number as the connection timeout, to spread out load.

key_flags.name: --oidc-ca-file
key_flags.description: If set, the OpenID server's certificate will be verified by one of the authorities in the oidc-ca-file, otherwise the host's root CA set will be used.

key_flags.name: --oidc-client-id
key_flags.description: The client ID for the OpenID Connect client, must be set if oidc-issuer-url is set.

key_flags.name: --oidc-groups-claim
key_flags.description: If provided, the name of a custom OpenID Connect claim for specifying user groups. The claim value is expected to be a string or array of strings. This flag is experimental, please see the authentication documentation for further details.

key_flags.name: --oidc-groups-prefix
key_flags.description: If provided, all groups will be prefixed with this value to prevent conflicts with other authentication strategies.

key_flags.name: --oidc-issuer-url
key_flags.description: The URL of the OpenID issuer, only HTTPS scheme will be accepted. If set, it will be used to verify the OIDC JSON Web Token (JWT).

key_flags.name: --oidc-required-claim
key_flags.description: A key=value pair that describes a required claim in the ID Token. If set, the claim is verified to be present in the ID Token with a matching value. Repeat this flag to specify multiple claims.

key_flags.name: --oidc-signing-algs
key_flags.description: Comma-separated list of allowed JOSE asymmetric signing algorithms. JWTs with a supported 'alg' header values are: RS256, RS384, RS512, ES256, ES384, ES512, PS256, PS384, PS512. Values are defined by RFC 7518 https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7518#section-3.1.

key_flags.name: --oidc-username-claim
key_flags.description: The OpenID claim to use as the user name. Note that claims other than the default ('sub') is not guaranteed to be unique and immutable. This flag is experimental, please see the authentication documentation for further details.

key_flags.name: --oidc-username-prefix
key_flags.description: If provided, all usernames will be prefixed with this value. If not provided, username claims other than 'email' are prefixed by the issuer URL to avoid clashes. To skip any prefixing, provide the value '-'.

key_flags.name: --peer-advertise-ip
key_flags.description: If set and the UnknownVersionInteroperabilityProxy feature gate is enabled, this IP will be used by peer kube-apiservers to proxy requests to this kube-apiserver when the request cannot be handled by the peer due to version skew between the kube-apiservers. This flag is only used in clusters configured with multiple kube-apiservers for high availability.

key_flags.name: --peer-advertise-port
key_flags.description: If set and the UnknownVersionInteroperabilityProxy feature gate is enabled, this port will be used by peer kube-apiservers to proxy requests to this kube-apiserver when the request cannot be handled by the peer due to version skew between the kube-apiservers. This flag is only used in clusters configured with multiple kube-apiservers for high availability.

key_flags.name: --peer-ca-file
key_flags.description: If set and the UnknownVersionInteroperabilityProxy feature gate is enabled, this file will be used to verify serving certificates of peer kube-apiservers. This flag is only used in clusters configured with multiple kube-apiservers for high availability.

key_flags.name: --permit-address-sharing
key_flags.description: If true, SO_REUSEADDR will be used when binding the port. This allows binding to wildcard IPs like 0.0.0.0 and specific IPs in parallel, and it avoids waiting for the kernel to release sockets in TIME_WAIT state. [default=false]

key_flags.name: --permit-port-sharing
key_flags.description: If true, SO_REUSEPORT will be used when binding the port, which allows more than one instance to bind on the same address and port. [default=false]

key_flags.name: --profiling
key_flags.description: Enable profiling via web interface host:port/debug/pprof/

key_flags.name: --proxy-client-cert-file
key_flags.description: Client certificate used to prove the identity of the aggregator or kube-apiserver when it must call out during a request. This includes proxying requests to a user api-server and calling out to webhook admission plugins. It is expected that this cert includes a signature from the CA in the --requestheader-client-ca-file flag. That CA is published in the 'extension-apiserver-authentication' configmap in the kube-system namespace. Components receiving calls from kube-aggregator should use that CA

key_flags.name: --proxy-client-key-file
key_flags.description: Private key for the client certificate used to prove the identity of the aggregator or kube-apiserver when it must call out during a request. This includes proxying requests to a user api-server and calling out to webhook admission plugins.

key_flags.name: --request-timeout
key_flags.description: An optional field indicating the duration a handler must keep a request open before timing it out. This is the default request timeout for requests but may be overridden by flags such as --min-request-timeout for specific types of requests.

key_flags.name: --requestheader-allowed-names
key_flags.description: List of client certificate common names to allow to provide usernames in headers specified by --requestheader-username-headers. If empty, any client certificate validated by the authorities in --requestheader-client-ca-file is allowed.

key_flags.name: --requestheader-client-ca-file
key_flags.description: Root certificate bundle to use to verify client certificates on incoming requests before trusting usernames in headers specified by --requestheader-username-headers. WARNING: generally do not depend on authorization being already done for incoming requests.

key_flags.name: --requestheader-extra-headers-prefix
key_flags.description: List of request header prefixes to inspect. X-Remote-Extra- is suggested.

key_flags.name: --requestheader-group-headers
key_flags.description: List of request headers to inspect for groups. X-Remote-Group is suggested.

key_flags.name: --requestheader-uid-headers
key_flags.description: List of request headers to inspect for UIDs. X-Remote-Uid is suggested. Requires the RemoteRequestHeaderUID feature to be enabled.

key_flags.name: --requestheader-username-headers
key_flags.description: List of request headers to inspect for usernames. X-Remote-User is common.

key_flags.name: --runtime-config
key_flags.description: A set of key=value pairs that enable or disable built-in APIs. key_flags.name: --runtime-config-emulation-forward-compatible
